title: DVR quotient augmentation, Koszul completion and open completeness
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] use its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], $B_{n,T}=(A_n)_T$ and $\widehat R_T=\lim_nB_{n,T}$. Use the strict semilinear module-system category $\mathscr S_T$, derived reduction $\mathcal R_T\dashv\mathcal L_T$, and the actual unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Completeness means the quotient-tower Roos-triangle condition of [def-weil-derived-complete], and normalized means that every transition-adjoint $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,T}}B_{n,T}\to N_n$ is invertible for $m\ge n$.

The pair $(R,(t))$ satisfies [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]: $R$ is Noetherian, $R/(t)$ is additive torsion, and each $A_n$ is finite and perfect over $R$, with finite-free resolution $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$. The canonical constant-sheaf comparison identifies $B_{n,T}$ with the sheafification of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|V|),A_n)$, including all quotient maps; its limit identifies $\widehat R_T$ with the sheaf $A_T$ of that datum [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction].

For every $P\in D(\widehat R_T)$, the strict quotient tower $P_\bullet$ of that datum is canonically the scalar restriction $U_T\mathcal R_TP$, and the canonical quotient completion map is the actual adjunction unit:
$$\operatorname{comp}_P=u_P:P\longrightarrow\mathcal L_T\mathcal R_TP.$$
On a single flat-term K-flat representative $Q$, the two maps have the same simultaneous representative: the strict augmentation from the constant tower $\Delta Q$, with components $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, before total derived limit [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For the intrinsic Koszul completion $P^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}}$, its map $\kappa_P$, and the specified comparison $c_P$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion, prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], one has
$$c_P\circ\kappa_P=u_P.$$
Quotient-tower completeness of $P$ is equivalent to invertibility of $\kappa_P$.

For every quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], localized extension by zero $j_!$ [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] sends every quotient-complete $K\in D(\widehat R_U)$ to a quotient-complete $j_!K$. The actual unit $u_{j_!K}=\operatorname{comp}_{j_!K}$ is invertible, and its composite with the total-limit Roos projection is the actual reduction map at each $n$. No boundedness, constructibility, finite-type hypothesis on the schemes, or commutation of $j_!$ with arbitrary inverse limits is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to the absolute value specified in the coefficient datum: $R$ is a domain and a principal ideal ring, $t\ne0$, and its residue field is finite. Every ideal is generated by one element, so $R$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] with this valuation ring and uniformizer to obtain finite $A_n$ and the stated quotient maps. The additive group of $R/(t)$ is finite; if its cardinality is $q$, the sequence $0,x,\ldots,qx$ has a repetition for every $x$, so a positive integer kills $x$. Multiplication by $t^n$ is injective since $R$ is a domain and $t\ne0$. Thus $[R\xrightarrow{t^n}R]$ has zero cohomology in degree $-1$ and cokernel $A_n$ in degree $0$. Its terms are rank-one free modules, hence finitely generated projective, so it is the required perfect resolution by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. These verify every ring hypothesis in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

source.place: Coefficient comparisons: verification of the DVR instance of the adic datum; elementary consequences of the cited arithmetic statements.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] for $(A,I)=(R,(t))$. Its finite-quotient clause identifies the locally constant sheaf $\underline{A_n}$ with the sheafification of $V\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|V|),A_n)$. For $m\ge n$, both descriptions of the quotient transition send a locally constant section $f$ to $q_{m,n}\circ f$; this equality before sheafification proves compatibility for the entire strict tower. The limit identification therefore respects every projection and gives $\widehat R_T=A_T$. Apply the resolution clause of the same lemma to the resolution in Step 1: $[\widehat R_T\xrightarrow{t^n}\widehat R_T]$ represents $B_{n,T}$. Consequently multiplication by $t^n$ on $\widehat R_T$ is injective and the canonical cokernel is $B_{n,T}$. In particular the regular-generator hypothesis needed below holds for $\mathcal O=\widehat R_T$ and $a=t$.

source.place: Tag 093M (lemma-completion-flat), applied to every power of (t); finite constant sheaf identification in the cited completed-coefficient lemma.

proof.text: Choose one flat-term K-flat resolution $Q\to P$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the strict quotient tower $P_\bullet$ is represented by $(Q\otimes_{\widehat R_T}B_{n,T})_n$, with transitions $1\otimes q_{m,n}$ and scalar restriction to $\widehat R_T$. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], exactly this same complex of semilinear systems represents $\mathcal R_TP$. Applying $U_T$ forgets only the quotient-ring actions, leaving those differentials and transitions unchanged. Thus the two strict derived towers are canonically identified, before applying evaluation or $R\lim$. Their strict augmentations from $\Delta Q$ are also identical: at every level the map is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and $(1\otimes q_{m,n})(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$.

source.place: The maps are tensor reassociation and adjunction units/counits: simultaneous strict quotient representative.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-sequence-projection-derived-adjunction] on the fixed small skeleton of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, with $A=\widehat R_T$, $B_n=B_{n,T}$ and structural maps the limit projections. Step 3 supplies its flat-term K-flat representative and its sheaf tensor model. The ordinary Hom correspondence sends $h:Q\to\lim_n\operatorname{Res}N_n$ to $(x\otimes b\mapsto b\pi_n h(x))_n$. For $N_n=Q\otimes B_{n,T}$ the identity of the strict system is therefore adjoint to $h(x)=(x\otimes1)_n$: its adjunct sends $x\otimes b$ to $b(x\otimes1)=x\otimes b$. This is the ordinary quotient-limit unit, not merely a family of maps after localization. That lemma specifies the derived correspondence as the derived fraction extension of this ordinary correspondence, and [lem-coef-sequence-pushforward-limit-projections] specifies transport from $Rp_*$ to the actual total $R\lim\,U_T$. Hence the derived unit is localization of this ordinary $h$, followed by the universal ordinary-limit-to-derived-limit comparison. On the same K-flat $Q$, [lem-weil-pbc-completed-quotient-unit-normalization] identifies precisely this composite with the derived constant/limit unit followed by $R\lim$ of the strict quotient augmentation. The latter is $\operatorname{comp}_P$ by [def-weil-pbc-completed-quotient-completion-unit]. Thus $u_P=\operatorname{comp}_P$. This comparison takes place on the whole strict augmentation; it does not infer equality from finite projections. Naturality of both derived constructions transports it from $Q$ to $P$.

source.place: The maps are tensor reassociation, evaluation, and adjunction units and counits: identify the actual integral quotient-completion unit.

proof.text: All hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] are now verified by Steps 1-3. Its specified comparison $c_P$ is an isomorphism and satisfies $c_P\kappa_P=\operatorname{comp}_P$. Substituting Step 4 proves $c_P\kappa_P=u_P$. The statement concerns the specified comparison of the Koszul and quotient towers, so no replacement by an arbitrary isomorphism of their limits is made.

source.place: Tag 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), through the cited completed-coefficient reconstruction theorem and its specified unit equation.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal O=\widehat R_T$. Step 2 identifies $B_{n,T}=\mathcal O/t^n\mathcal O$ and proves $t$ regular. For the K-flat $Q$ of Step 3, [lem-pur-derived-complete-koszul-reconstruction] therefore applies to exactly these strict reductions. If $P$ is quotient-complete in the Roos-triangle convention of [def-weil-derived-complete], its second assertion gives an isomorphism $P\simeq C_t(P)$, where $C_t(P)=R\lim_n(P\otimes^L[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t^n}\mathcal O])$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], $C_t(P)$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete. This property is invariant under isomorphisms: restriction and derived internal Hom send an isomorphism to an isomorphism. Thus $P$ is locally derived $(t)$-complete. The last equivalence in the reflector theorem makes its actual Koszul unit $\kappa_P$ invertible. We used the existence of $P\simeq C_t(P)$ only to transport completeness; we did not identify that possibly noncanonical isomorphism with $\kappa_P$.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion) and 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul): reflector argument for the existential Roos convention.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\kappa_P$ is invertible. Step 5 and invertibility of $c_P$ give invertibility of $\operatorname{comp}_P=u_P$. The canonical total-limit Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] has first map $\iota:R\lim P_\bullet\to\prod_n^D P_n$. By [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], the components of $\iota u_P$ are the actual reductions $P\to\operatorname{Res}_n P_n$. Transporting this distinguished triangle along the isomorphism $u_P$ gives the triangle required by [def-weil-derived-complete]. This proves quotient completeness. Together with Step 6, this gives both directions of the equivalence and also proves that the actual unit is invertible for every quotient-complete object.

source.place: Tag 0A0E: passage back from the specified completion unit to the quotient Roos triangle.

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be as stated and let $K$ be quotient-complete. Step 6 makes $K$ intrinsically $(t)$-complete. Apply [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] with $(A,I)=(R,(t))$ to the cartesian square having $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, $g_U=\mathrm{id}_U$ and $j'=j$. Its hypotheses require the adic datum and quasi-compactness of $j$, both already available, and its first conclusion says that the ordinary localized ringed extension $j_!K$ is intrinsically complete. This is the same extension functor as in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]: both use exact extension on the slice with coefficient ring $\widehat R_X|_U=\widehat R_U$. Step 7 now gives quotient completeness of $j_!K$ and invertibility of its actual $u_{j_!K}=\operatorname{comp}_{j_!K}$. Finally the unit/projection equation in [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives its actual reduction map at every $n$. The cited open theorem assumes quasi-compactness of the immersion but no boundedness, constructibility, finite type of either scheme, or independent inverse-limit commutation hypothesis.
